patch.design_goal: Three compact bone-corridor dilemmas with immediate, surgical tone and visible risk/reward using only existing actions.

event.line_1: Lamella lifts; plate-buds click, hungry to fuse.
event.line_2: Graft now, or wake the ward to claim the aisle.
event.speaker: Her

event.line_1: A ridge-lathe shaves calcium, steady and clean.
event.line_2: Lean in for spurs, or jam it and face what comes.
event.speaker: Her

event.line_1: The shaft pinches; osteal barbs taste my heat.
event.line_2: Force the choke, call a hunter, or withdraw.
event.speaker: Her

inspiration_notes: Clinical hazard framing with bodily machinery.
Ritual sacrifice tone condensed into moment-to-moment choices.
Roguelike clarity: meaningful, legible tradeoffs under pressure.
self_critique: Kept to existing actions; no hidden mechanics assumed.
Risk/reward is signposted but depends on core handlers for payoff.
Language is tight; avoids lore dumps while keeping surgical texture.
patch.title: Bone Corridor: Sharp Passages

patch.design_goal: Two amber_corridor resource events with concrete amber gain and visible bodily risk, using existing actions only.

event.line_1: Amber pulses in the stem. I can siphon a jarful.
event.line_2: The vein is hot; a slip will flood the wound.
event.speaker: Her

event.line_1: A split gland leaks thick amber onto the floor.
event.line_2: I can seal it, or cut deeper and take the full clump.
event.speaker: Her

inspiration_notes: Concrete material payoff: a jarful, a clump, a leaking gland.
Visible risk is immediate in the text: hot vein, flooding wound, floor leak.
Room-appropriate verbs kept tight: siphon, seal, cut, leave.
self_critique: Both events stay within existing resource actions only.
Second event uses seal_amber_wound for safety and siphon_amber for greed, but the exact yield split depends on the handler.
Text remains compact and playable, with no unsupported delayed effects.
patch.title: Amber Corridor: Two Clear Strips

patch.design_goal: Two amber_corridor resource events in first-person degraded field-report voice. One is a controlled siphon with contained risk and modest, concrete gain. The other is a greedy extraction with visible instability, higher pressure, and refusal framed as lost opportunity. Existing actions only.

event.line_1: Pressure conduit. Amber bead in the valve-teeth.
event.line_2: Measured draw keeps the seal alive. Wait too long and it bites shut.
event.speaker: Her

event.line_1: Reservoir gland blown open. Amber venting through the split.
event.line_2: Hard draw strips more mass. The valve spasms. Heat goes into my hands.
event.speaker: Her

inspiration_notes: Controlled extraction is framed as stable, quiet work with lower damage and lower yield.
Greedy extraction is framed as an overdraw from a pressurized gland with higher damage, higher yield, and danger from overdraw_amber.
Refusal is not neutral: it means forfeiting a draw or abandoning a rich seam.
Text stays clipped, first-person, and transactional, with room-appropriate verbs.
The greedy event now uses overdraw_amber, a supported high-risk amber action.
self_critique: The controlled event is low-risk harvest; the greedy event is a pressured overdraw with implied danger.
I set event damage and biomass fields so the controlled and greedy choices differ mechanically.
The greedy event uses overdraw_amber, so the higher danger is mechanical instead of only textual.
patch.title: Amber Corridor: Controlled and Greedy Extraction
